segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ מְשַׁלְּחִין כֵּלִים בֵּין תְּפוּרִין בֵּין שֶׁאֵינָן תְּפוּרִין, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן כִּלְאַיִם וְהֵן לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד. אֲבָל לֹא סַנְדָּל הַמְסוּמָּר וְלֹא מִנְעָל שֶׁאֵינוֹ תָּפוּר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף לֹא מִנְעָל לָבָן, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ אוּמָּן. זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל שֶׁנֵּאוֹתִין בּוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב — מְשַׁלְּחִין אוֹתוֹ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One may send clothes, whether» they are «sewn or whether they are unsewn, and even if they contain diverse kinds,» a prohibited mixture of wool and linen [sha’atnez]. «But» one may do so only if «they» serve «the purposes of the Festival. However, one may not» send «a spiked sandal,» which has nails fixed to it, as the Sages decreed that one may not wear a sandal of this kind on a Shabbat or Festival, «nor an unsewn shoe,» which is not suitable for a Festival. «Rabbi Yehuda says: One may not even» send «a white shoe,» which people do not usually wear, «because» it «requires an artisan» to paint it black. «This is the» general «principle:» Anything «that one may use on a Festival, one may send it.»
